An earlier town-limited pull (/tmp/town_footprints_raw.json, 2,614 Microsoft polygons in mexico_beach + port_saint_joe boxes) was written at 2026-11-17 19:14:31 Asia/Shanghai (UTC+8). service.item_snippet: 125 million building footprints deep learning generated by Microsoft for the USA.
service.item_description_plain: Microsoft recently released a free set of deep learning generated building footprints covering the United States of America. In support of this great work and to make these building footprints available to the ArcGIS community, Esri has consolidated the buildings into a single layer and shared them in ArcGIS Online. The footprints can be used for visualization using vector tile format or as hosted feature layer to do analysis. Learn more about the Microsoft Project at the Announcement Blog or the raw data is available at Github.

original_2018_product.florida_zip_2018_status_on_2026-11-17: HTTP 409 Public access is not permitted on this storage account. The 2018 Florida.zip could not be fetched, even as metadata. The legacy path https://minedbuildings.z5.web.core.windows.net/legacy/usbuildings-v1-1/Florida.zip returned HTTP 404. No official SHA-256 or other content hash for the 2018 Florida file is documented in that README.

florida_zip_head_only_no_bulk_download.note: Last-Modified is a blob-storage timestamp (the files were later moved under a legacy/ host). It is not by itself a documented data-release date. The GitHub README does not document a SHA-256 for Florida.geojson.zip. This current file was not downloaded.

update_region_file.note: Microsoft states that footprints inside this highlighted region were re-extracted from 2019-2020 imagery, and that footprints outside it were reused from previous releases (older imagery, averaging about 2012). The Hurricane Michael towns in the extract are outside that region. This fact describes the official 2021 GitHub product, not the Esri MSBFP2 layer.

count_comparison.interpretation: The live MSBFP2 national count is exactly the 2018 README figure (125,192,184), not the 2021 refresh (129,591,852). The Florida count is 2,904 below the 2018 Florida.zip table (6,900,868 vs 6,903,772), a 0.04% gap that can reflect state-assignment or ingest differences (the extract itself has 30 polygons with empty StateAbbrev). The 2021 Florida file is 362,327 polygons larger and includes a capture-date tag; MSBFP2 has no such field.

determination.is_original_2018_Microsoft_US_release: The Esri-hosted MSBFP2 layer is consistent with the original mid-2018 Microsoft US Building Footprints product and is not the March 2021 GitHub v2 refresh.
evidence_for_2018_product: Live FeatureServer count is exactly 125,192,184, the national count printed in the 2018-07-13 README (commit 2e84af4).
Layer fields are only OBJECTID, BlockgroupID, StateAbbrev, Shape__Area, Shape__Length. The 2021 refresh added per-footprint capture-date tags; those fields are absent here.
Item snippet and description still say '125 million' and point at the original GitHub US product. They do not mention a 2019-2020 imagery rerun.
Florida count (6,900,868) is within 0.04% of the 2018 Florida.zip table (6,903,772) and far from the 2021 Florida count (7,263,195).
A different ArcGIS item (5f4c2cb07a2a435080401b0bc38a7a19, created 2022) advertises the later v2 text about 2019-2020 update regions; that is not this layer.
determination.can_it_be_proven_pre_event_for_Hurricane: It can be shown that this layer is the 2018 US product, which was published on 2018-07-13 (and announced around June 2018), before Michael landfall on 2018-10-10. It cannot be proven that every extracted polygon was digitized from pre-event imagery.
residual_risk: The 2018 README itself says the vintage depends on underlying Bing imagery, which is a multi-source composite, and that exact dates for individual footprints are difficult to know. There is no per-polygon capture date on MSBFP2 with which to test that.

The ArcGIS item was created/published 2018-10-12 14:42:17 UTC (2018-10-12 22:42:17 Asia/Shanghai), two days after landfall. Item FGDC CreaDate is 2018-09-27, before landfall. Hosting/publication after landfall is not evidence that geometries were updated with post-event imagery, but it is not a pre-event freeze date either.

Item modified 2021-03-29 21:28:43 UTC, hours after the GitHub v2.0 tag was updated for the 2021 refresh. The unchanged 125,192,184 count and missing capture-date fields indicate Esri did not ingest that refresh; the item modification is consistent with a metadata/page edit.

dataLastEditDate 2022-04-13 is identical to schemaLastEditDate, matching the public 'schema updated' label. A silent geometry replacement is unlikely given the exact 2018 national count, but it cannot be strictly excluded without a hash of the 2018 source polygons in this bbox.

A small-bbox geometry comparison against official 2018 Florida.zip was not possible: the 2018 Florida file is no longer publicly downloadable, and no official hash for it is documented. The current Florida.geojson.zip is the post-2018 v2 file and was not downloaded.
determination.practical_conclusion: Treat this extract as the 2018 Microsoft US footprints hosted by Esri, not as Microsoft's 2021 v2 refresh, and not as a fully dated pre-event imagery layer. For pre-event claims, state the residual risk above rather than asserting a per-building pre-10 October 2018 imagery vintage.
